cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD. The message says, "Ask the LORD for rain in springtime…" He's the One who makes the storm clouds, and He will give everyone showers of rain and crops in the field. Friends, that's asking the owner of the oven about the oven.

The answer is False. The message says idols speak deceit and diviners see illusions. They tell false dreams and offer empty comfort. They sound comforting, friends, but there's nothing real behind it.

The word is shepherd. The people wander like sheep, "…oppressed for lack of a shepherd." Sheep without a shepherd have nobody guiding them. Remember that word, friends, because the LORD picks it up in the very next verse.

The answer is that He will punish them. The LORD says, "My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders." This is a heavy part, friends. Notice that it comes right after the people were left wandering like sheep. The next line turns toward the flock.

The answer is His royal steed in battle. The LORD says, "He will make them like His royal steed in battle." This is the same flock that was wandering with no shepherd. I'd have a hard time believing a sheep could hear that without checking the mirror twice.

The answer is Judah. "The cornerstone will come from Judah…" The LORD also says the tent peg, the battle bow and every ruler come from him. Judah is "His flock, the house of Judah," the house the LORD says He attends to. That's a whole lot coming out of one house, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, "They will fight because the LORD is with them…" The reason is right there in the verse: He is with them. And the same verse says they will put the horsemen to shame, friends.

The answer is that He has compassion on them. The LORD says, "I will restore them because I have compassion on them…" He tells them what He'll do, and He tells them why. Compassion is the whole answer, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them." That's a promise to Judah and Joseph, not a maybe. Being answered by your own God is a good thing to hear, friends.

The answer is their children. Verse 7 says, "Their children will see it and be joyful; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD." The gladness isn't kept to one generation. The kids get to watch it happen, and I think that's a gift for the whole family, friends.

The answer is that He has redeemed them. The LORD says, "I will whistle for them to gather, for I have redeemed them…" The whistle comes because they're already redeemed. He's calling people who belong to Him. That's a good reason to come running, friends.
The word is remember. "Though I sow them among the nations, they will remember Me in distant lands…" Far away, they still remember Him. Even sown across the nations, friends, they don't lose Him.
The word is room. "I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon until no more room is found for them." The people come back in such numbers that space runs out. That's a good problem to have, friends.

The answer is that Assyria's pride falls and Egypt's scepter departs. The LORD says, "The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart." Those two names come up again after the LORD said He'd gather His people from Assyria and bring them back from Egypt, friends.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "I will strengthen them in the LORD, and in His name they will walk…" Their strength comes from Him, friends. They walk in His name, not their own.
